subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.

requests.what: Maker's emblem on the anvil's front waist: a raised brass hammer-and-crown crest in a small shield plate, with four rivets. Colours BRASS, STEEL_DARK.
Tool pocket on the lower apron: a stitched LEATHER_DARK pouch with flap, brass rivets, and the handles of a small chisel and file poking out.
Glowing EMBER dwarven runes inlaid on both faces of the hammer head, a brass band at each end, and a wrapped leather grip with a pommel cap on the handle.
Ornament for both pauldrons: a ring of three or four STEEL_LIGHT cone spikes, rivet studs round the rim and a brass trim band.
Big square brass belt buckle with an embossed anvil emblem, plus small hanging pouch, ring and key on the belt sides.
Crest on top of the helm: a ridge fin of BEARD_DARK bristles from front to back, with a brass cap plate and rivets along its base.
Tongs detail where the tongs grip the ingot: shaped STEEL_DARK jaws, a pivot rivet and curved ends. Plus a few extra glowing HOT sparks drifting above.
Details on the anvil stump front: a hatchet buried in the top edge, wood chips and chisel nicks, scorch-black patches, and iron nails on the hoops.
Straps on both boots: two BRASS buckled straps across the ankle and a folded leather cuff with stitching at the top.
Brass and steel beard rings clasping the braids and the tips of the beard, with a small bone bead on each braid, and two thin extra braids beside the mouth.
Goggles polish: leather strap round the helm, small brass wing-nuts, lens glass glints and a cracked corner.
Worn leather: darker scorch and soot blotches near the bottom, hammered grease stains, stitched seams at edges, in LEATHER and LEATHER_DARK.
Beard hair: long vertical strands in BEARD, BEARD_LIGHT streaks and BEARD_DARK roots, with a few grey-white streaks near the chin.
Hammered steel face: bright polished centre with dents, dark scorch edges and faint orange heat tint near the middle, in STEEL, STEEL_LIGHT, STEEL_DARK.
Stump: bark grain on the sides in WOOD and WOOD_DARK with moss-free cracks, charred top with ring pattern and hammer dents.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith character at an anvil—chunky build, braided beard, helmet with goggles, leather apron, hammer, and a glowing ingot—aiming to keep the module compact at around 250 lines with simple joint and part structures for SDK correctness.

I'm mapping out the skeleton with hips, spine, chest, neck, head, and jaw joints positioned along a roughly 1.45m tall frame, then starting on arm and leg joint chains for the limbs.

For the arms, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints parented to the chest with a slight outward neutral pose, planning for the right hand to hold the hammer and the left to possibly hold tongs.

I'm positioning the hammer so its handle runs diagonally from the hand toward the anvil, with the head angled up near the anvil's surface. Now I'm setting sweep radii for the limbs and considering sleeve coverings over the upper arm using a cloth color.

Sketching leg joints...

For boots, I'll sweep thick geometry over the lower leg with the foot as a separate box sitting at ankle height, checking the bottom aligns flush with the floor at y=0. For the torso, I'm using scaled sphere/box primitives for chest, belly, and hips rather than a full loft, adding steel pauldron spheres at the shoulders and a leather apron box up front with a belt.

Now I'm layering the big dwarf beard with cones and boxes in auburn tones, adding downward-tapering spikes, braided catmull sweeps with ring ties, curved mustache sweeps, a bulbous nose sphere, simple eye spheres with pupils, thick brow boxes, and a partial-sphere steel helmet dome using thetaLength to shape the bowl.

Still roughing out head proportions...

Adding jaw position and tilted eyebrow boxes, then building the beard as a layered sphere with spike tufts hanging to chest height, plus braid sweeps extending down from the jaw sides.

Now sketching tie bands, a curved mustache using catmull splines on the head bone, a small dark mouth slit, pointed ear spheres, and the anvil setup with a wooden stump and a boxy anvil base.

Adding the anvil face with a horn spike pointing toward +X, plus a heel box on the -X end. I'm placing a glowing orange ingot on the anvil surface with sparks as small glowing spheres, using the ember glow kit import. I'm skipping the bucket but adding tongs as two rods connecting the left hand to the ingot.

Now I'm positioning the hammer in the right hand with a handle rod leading to a box-shaped head oriented along the x-axis, plus steel cylinder caps and a fist sphere for the hand, and starting on a leather apron box.

For the apron, I'm extruding a trapezoid outline in front of the torso's belly, positioning it at the proper z-depth so it clears the belly sphere, with the bib narrowing toward the top between y 0.45 and 1.12.

I'm thinking about attaching the apron to a spine bone, adding strap sweeps up to the shoulders, a small extruded pocket, and tiny rivet spheres, keeping the apron fairly plain since texture and an emblem will come via a later request. Now I'm working out the belt geometry, considering whether to use a scaled cylinder or torus shape for it.

Belt sits as a scaled cylinder at the belly level, sized to wrap snugly, with a brass buckle box positioned in front. But since the apron sits closer to the viewer, it would actually hide the belt buckle, so I'm reconsidering the layering so the belt shows over the apron instead.

Now I'm shifting focus to the shoulders, adding pauldron spheres with spike studs on top for a bone-chest look, then sketching out the sleeve sweeps so the arm cloth drapes correctly.

For torso I'm scaling a shirt-colored chest sphere at the collar position and skipping chest hair detail; the neck is a simple skin cylinder hidden behind the beard. For hands I'm using fist spheres with a small thumb sphere rather than individual fingers, plus gauntlet bracers built as rods running along the forearm between elbow and wrist points.

Now I'm defining the boots and legs: using a swept shape along the leg chain with color bands switching from pants to boot material around the knee, tapering the radius from thigh to ankle, and adding boot boxes at the foot positions for width and length.

For the ankle I'm attaching a cuff ring with a small brass buckle and a thin dark sole box, bound to the appropriate leg joint in the chain. For parts not on the main chain, I'm using a bone parameter tied to named joint objects instead.

For the head, I'm building a hemisphere helmet scaled and positioned above the head bone, accepting that the open bottom won't be visible from normal viewing angles, plus a brim band using a short cylinder ring around the base.

I'm skipping the nasal guard since it'd sit awkwardly in front of the face, and instead adding curved horn spikes swept along bezier curves from the sides of the helmet outward and upward, colored like bone and bound to the head joint. I'm also considering rivet studs as a ring of small spheres along the helmet's rim.

For the goggles, I'm placing them pushed up onto the helmet's forehead area, calculating the surface position on the helmet sphere to determine where they protrude, then adding two brass cylinders with blue glowing lens discs oriented to sit flush against the curved surface.

Working out eye placement relative to the head sphere's surface geometry, then positioning the nose and cheek spheres with slight redder skin tones. I'm also setting up the jaw bone to anchor the beard, parenting it to the head joint and aiming it forward and down.

Now I'm sizing the beard as a large flattened sphere covering the lower face, with extra cheek spheres blending the sides, and a small skin box hidden mostly underneath. I'm carving out a tiny dark mouth cavity positioned so it falls inside the beard's front coverage, checking that the beard sphere's span naturally hides the jaw while leaving the mouth visible at its front edge.

Now I'm adding color options to the spike helper so beard spikes get a bone-jaw attachment and gradient tint, then working out the braids as catmull-rom curves sweeping down from the sides of the beard with small sphere knots placed along the path using a `.at(t)` sampling method.

I'm checking where the braid ends collide with the apron and belly geometry — nudging the braid's z-depth outward at a few points (.26, .3, .335) so they clear the belly sphere and sit over the apron bib instead of poking through it.

Now I'm thinking about small accent requests to add: an anvil maker's mark positioned on the front face, an apron pocket detail, and runic etchings on the hammer head, each placed with a normal direction and bounding room size so the decal generator knows where to project them.

I'm also working through more placements — pauldron ornaments, a belt buckle emblem, helmet crest, tongs detail near the hand, boot strap accents, glowing embers above the ingot, and an axe-stump band detail with iron chips — plus starting to note the texture list beginning with apron leather and beard material.

Now I'm settling on part names (apron, beardMain, anvilTop, stump) and sketching out the build code: importing the glow helper, setting up color constants, and writing a small wrapper function to simplify creating parts with bone attachments and positions, along with geometry helper functions for shapes like spheres.

Arm and leg chains come next—I'm planning three-point catmull chains for arms (shoulder, elbow, hand) with left/right mirroring via a sign flag, and four-joint chains for legs (hip, knee, ankle, toe), all parented to the chest and hips joints respectively.

Head placement follows: a neck joint under the chest, head above that, and jaw under head, with sleeve bands transitioning from shirt color to skin color along the arm sweep, ending in fist spheres positioned at each wrist.

Now I'm working out the hammer: a wooden rod running from the wrist angled forward to a steel head block capped with darker cylindrical faces, attached to the arm's tip bone. For the tongs on the other side, I'm placing two parallel offset rods from the wrist up to a pinch point meant to grip an ingot.

I'm fixing the ingot position relative to the anvil surface, making sure its height sits just below where the tongs clamp, plus a small rivet sphere detail at the joint. For the anvil itself, I'm building a flat base box and a cylindrical stump beneath it, deciding to bind the whole prop to the hips/root bone for simplicity even though it's a static object.

Now I'm adding the waist section, face plate, and a cone-shaped horn with a slightly tilted upward direction, adjusting the horn's radius down to better match its height, plus a heel box extending to one side.

Continuing, I'm placing a small dark hardy hole box on the face's top, naming the lighter top plate "anvilTop," and adding iron hoop rings around the stump using slightly larger cylinders at two heights. I'm also positioning the dwarf's feet and toes relative to the stump's back.

Now I'm adding shoulder straps as thin leather rods connecting the apron's bib to points behind the shoulders, then shaping steel pauldrons from hemisphere geometries placed at each shoulder, tilting them outward with a rotation around the z-axis to flare the tops away from the body.

Beyond that I'm positioning the boots and soles so the feet sit flush with the ground, keeping the boot box just above a slightly recessed sole, and leaving small details like rim studs and spikes for a later stage.

Now I'm adding facial and head features: dark beard-matching eyebrows, side and back hair tufts peeking from under the helmet, and small pointed ears sized as thin ellipsoids near the temples, all tied to a ruddy dwarf skin tone.

Setting up the full color palette now—auburn beard with highlight and shadow tones, Ironforge blue shirt, leather browns, steel and brass metallics, glowing orange accents, and wood/pants tones. Writing beard spike loop code...

Placing the mouth box slightly in front of the beard sphere so the lower lip peeks out, dark red and small, with the mustache above hiding the top edge. Now I'm setting up the spark/ember glow wrapper and moving into stage 2 of the loop, defining radii for the chain sweep and making sure to give explicit colors alongside the bands rather than relying on nearest-match defaults, then starting on limb roles.
